newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's AMP float to cost A$50-100 mln.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's AMP float to cost A$50-100 mln.

text.p: The Australian Mutual Provident Society (AMP) said on Thursday it expected the float process to cost at least A$50 million to A$100 million and it had already spent A$10 million evaluating the process.

"We spent a little over A$10 million last year on the evaluation and in the first stage we would estimate we will spend somewhere between A$50 and A$100 million. In the next stage beyond that with actual listing and getting shares to 2.5 million people, we haven't figured that out yet," managing director George Trumbull told a news conference.

AMP, Australia's largest insurance group and largest institutional investor, earlier on Thursday said it would recommend to members that it demutualise with a listing on the Australian Stock Exchange in mid-to-late 1998.
The society said it also planned to list in New Zealand and possibly the United Kingdom.
